data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense fails because it conflates 'acting on a known falsehood' with 'preferring one non-refuted theory over another.' Popper's problem arises precisely when multiple theories have survived severe tests (are all 'not yet known to be wrong'), yet scientists still prefer the better-corroborated one. The target claims we prefer the corroborated theory simply because the alternative is 'proven false or untested,' which ignores the core dilemma of choosing between two unfalsified rivals where the 'error elimination' logic provides no basis for preference.
